questions.questionText: The policyowner, age 50, has been paying the premiums on his whole life policy for fifteen years. He needs the equivalent of one-third of his policy's cash value for two years. He wants to continue to have the same amount of life insurance protection and he can afford to continue to pay the policy's premium. Which of the following would appear to be his BEST course of action?

choices.text: Look elsewhere. Whole Life policies do not develop cash value.
Use the policy loan provision to borrow money from the policy, but keep making the premium payments to keep the policy in force.
Surrender the policy, because to get any of the cash he must surrender the policy. He can then buy a new policy with the other two-thirds of the proceeds.
Look elsewhere. The insurer is not required to make the cash value available to the policyowner until the policy matures. If they allowed this, most policies would lapse.
